case_name: Sanjaybhai Chandulal Parekh v State of Gujarat and another
respondent:
State of Gujarat and another
Supreme Court of India

7 April 2017
Criminal Appeal No. 672 of 2017, (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 594/2017)
The Order of the Court was as follows :
1. Leave granted.
2. This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25.11.2016 passed by the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad, whereby the High Court dismissed the Criminal Misc. Application No. 30913 of 2016 preferred by the appellant herein under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 seeking quashing of FIR filed against him for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The only question which arises for our consideration is whether the FIR under challenge deserves to be quashed by the High Court.
4. The facts of the case, in brief, are as under:
(i) An FIR was registered at the instance of the Complainant / Respondent No.2 at P.S. Kanbha, District Ahmedabad under Sections 406, 420 and 120B of the IPC aga
facts: The FIR was registered at the instance of the Complainant / Respondent No.2 at P.S. Kanbha, District Ahmedabad under Sections 406, 420 and 120B of the IPC against the appellant and other accused alleging that the land in question belongs to Nilakanth Mahadev Mandir.
The Accused Nos. 1 to 5 were the administrators of the said property and that they only had the right to manage property, however no right to sell the property was ever given to them.

The property in question was sold by the above accused persons to one Pratapbhai Dahyabhai Parmar (Accused No.6) for a consideration of Rs.1,90,000/- by executing a registered sale deed in his favour.
The above Accused No.6 sold the above land to the appel- lant-herein for a consideration of Rs.10,55,000/- by a registered sale deed executed on 21.12.2015.
The Learned Judicial Magistrate, Ahmedabad enlarged the appellant on bail on 02.06.2016.
The appellant preferred a petition under Section 482 of the Code before the High Court seeking quashing of the above FIR against him.
The High Court by the impugned judgment dismissed the same.
issues: Whether the FIR under challenge deserves to be quashed by the High Court.
petitioner_arguments: No allegations whatsoever constituting the offences mentioned therein have been made against the appellant.

In the entire FIR there is not even a single averment against the appellant that he had purchased the property with any knowledge or dishonest or wrongful intention or has entered into any conspiracy with other accused persons and the FIR under challenge ought to have been quashed by the High Court in view of the facts which clearly goes to show that the same is an abuse of process of criminal law.
respondent_arguments: A prima facie case is made out for the purpose of investigation having regard to the nature of the allegations which disclose commission of a cognizable offence and the High Court was right in dismissing the application preferred by the appellant.
court_reasoning: The FIR, it is clear that no allegations whatsoever constituting the above offences have been made against the appellant.

In our opinion, the High Court while deciding the petition seeking quashing of FIR under Section 482 CR.P.C. has to appreciate the contents of the FIR and the material on record to form an opinion as to whether the offences as alleged in the FIR are even prima facie made out or not.
The prosecution of the appellant under Sections 406, 420 and 120B IPC is liable to be quashed.
holding: The FIR qua the appellant herein is quashed.
cases_cited: Sanjaybhai Chandulal Parekh v State of Gujarat
